newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Sigcau gives privatisation targets.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Sigcau gives privatisation targets.

text.p: South African Minister of Public Enterprises Stella Sigcau said in remarks published on Sunday that seven public sector corporations would be at least partly privatised by the end of next year.

The Johannesburg-based Sunday Times quoted Sigcau as saying in an interview that tourist resort group Aventura, mining group Alexcor, airline Sun Air and transport group Autonet would be fully privatised.
Strategic equity partners would have slices of telecommunications utility Telkom, the Airports Company which runs South Africa's major airports, and forestry group Safcol, Sigcau told the paper.
She said South African Airways would seek a foreign equity partner by the middle of 1998.
"We will continue to consult but are now primarily looking at ways of fast-tracking the privatisation process," she was quoted as saying.
In an apparent reference to criticism of the slow pace of privatisation so far, Sigcau said:
"There is no understanding of the complexity of the process involved. We have to tread carefully to ensure consensus, which has now been achieved."
